::: {.section-intro}
## Thirty questions for researchers

Every answer below is drawn from a page on this site, and every explanation links back to
the note it came from. The questions deliberately target the distinctions this project
works hardest to keep straight: hypo- versus hypermethylation, association versus
mechanism, assay development versus plate acceptance, and a surveillance threshold versus
a prediction.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="How to read your score"}
This is self-assessment against the site's own text, not an examination and not clinical
guidance. A missed question usually points at a page worth rereading rather than at a
fact worth memorising.
:::

    {

      stem: "Bill depth and body mass correlate at −0.472 across the penguin dataset, but at +0.576, +0.604 and +0.719 within each species. What is the right response?",
      options: [
        "Stratify — the fix is the stratification, not the statistic",
        "Switch to a rank-based statistic, which is immune to the problem",
        "Report the pooled estimate, since it uses all the data",
        "Discard the smallest species and recompute"
      ],
      answer: 0,
      explain: "This is Simpson's paradox: the pooled sign reverses because species is a confounder. No choice of correlation coefficient repairs it — the fix is the stratification, not the statistic. The same logic applies to cell composition and batch in methylation data.",
      href: "posts/beyond-correlation-association-vs-concordance/index.html",
      hrefText: "Beyond correlation: association versus concordance"
    },
    {
      theme: "Statistics",
      stem: "A test with 85% sensitivity and 90% specificity is applied where dysplasia prevalence is 5%, then where it is 12.5%. How does positive predictive value change?",
      options: [
        "It stays near 85%, because sensitivity is unchanged",
        "It rises from about 31% to about 55%",
        "It falls from about 55% to about 31%",
        "PPV does not depend on prevalence"
      ],
      answer: 1,
      explain: "At 5% prevalence the PPV is near 31% — about three colonoscopies per true finding. At the 12.5% dysplasia rate observed in a Latin American surveillance series of 144 colonoscopies, the same test returns roughly 55%. This is exact Bayes arithmetic and holds for any test with those characteristics, including tests that do not exist.",
      href: "posts/clinical-applications-of-methylation-siga-fingerprint/index.html",
      hrefText: "Could a blood draw ever replace part of a colonoscopy?"
    },
    {
      theme: "Statistics",
      stem: "A classifier is cross-validated on DMRs that were called once on the complete cohort. What is wrong?",
      options: [
        "It leaks outcome information into every test fold; feature discovery must be repeated within each training fold, or the feature set locked separately",
        "Nothing, provided the folds are stratified by group",
        "The error is only in the choice of classifier, not the procedure",
        "It is acceptable if the false-discovery rate was controlled during DMR calling"
      ],
      answer: 0,
      explain: "Calling DMRs on the complete cohort and then cross-validating leaks outcome information into every test fold. All outcome-aware steps — DMR discovery, imputation, scaling, feature selection, tuning — belong inside the training split, and tissue, plasma and every technical replicate from one participant must stay in the same fold.",
      href: "posts/statistical-analysis-of-methylation-data.html",
      hrefText: "Statistical analysis of methylation data"
    },
    {
      theme: "Clinical",
      stem: "When do the cited guidelines recommend beginning endoscopic dysplasia surveillance in long-standing ulcerative colitis?",
      options: [
        "At diagnosis, then annually for life",
        "Twenty years after diagnosis, regardless of disease extent",
        "Only once symptoms such as bleeding or weight loss appear",
        "AGA: about 8–10 years after diagnosis, earlier when PSC is present; ECCO: a screening colonoscopy eight years after the onset of first symptoms"
      ],
      answer: 3,
      explain: "The AGA advises beginning dysplasia screening about 8–10 years after diagnosis unless primary sclerosing cholangitis is present, when surveillance starts earlier; ECCO recommends a screening colonoscopy eight years after the onset of first symptoms. Surveillance is intended to find dysplasia or cancer even when symptoms are absent.",
      href: "posts/from-colitis-to-colorectal-cancer.html",
      hrefText: "From colitis to colorectal cancer"
    },
    {
      theme: "Clinical",
      stem: "What does the eight-year mark actually represent?",
      options: [
        "A prediction that cancer develops around eight years after diagnosis",
        "A surveillance threshold — cancer can occur earlier, later, or never",
        "The point at which surveillance can safely stop",
        "The median survival after a colitis-associated cancer diagnosis"
      ],
      answer: 1,
      explain: "The eight-year point is a surveillance threshold, not a prediction that cancer develops in eight years — cancer can occur earlier, later, or never, and most people with UC do not develop colorectal cancer. In the longest-running surveillance cohort, 72 of 1,375 patients developed CRC over 15,234 patient-years, an incidence of 4.7 per 1,000 patient-years.",
      href: "posts/from-colitis-to-colorectal-cancer.html",
      hrefText: "From colitis to colorectal cancer",
      href2: "posts/clinical-applications-of-methylation-siga-fingerprint/index.html",
      hrefText2: "Could a blood draw ever replace part of a colonoscopy?"
    },
    {
      theme: "Clinical",
      stem: "Beyond disease duration, which factors refine an individual's risk of colitis-associated colorectal cancer?",
      options: [
        "Disease extent, cumulative inflammatory burden, PSC, family history, stricture and prior dysplasia",
        "Age at first colonoscopy and body mass index alone",
        "Only the presence of active symptoms",
        "Serum sIgA concentration, which sets a validated risk threshold"
      ],
      answer: 0,
      explain: "Duration identifies when surveillance becomes especially important, but disease extent, cumulative inflammatory burden, PSC, family history, stricture, prior dysplasia and examination quality refine the risk. Dysplasia is the key established precursor finding; there is no validated sIgA threshold that predicts an individual's cancer risk.",
      href: "posts/from-colitis-to-colorectal-cancer.html",
      hrefText: "From colitis to colorectal cancer"
    }
  ];

  var shell = document.getElementById("qz-shell");
  if (!shell) return;
  var elTheme = document.getElementById("qz-theme");
  var elCount = document.getElementById("qz-count");
  var elScore = document.getElementById("qz-score");
  var elFill = document.getElementById("qz-progress-fill");
  var elStem = document.getElementById("qz-stem");
  var elOptions = document.getElementById("qz-options");
  var elFeedback = document.getElementById("qz-feedback");
  var elCheck = document.getElementById("qz-check");
  var elNext = document.getElementById("qz-next");
  var elResults = document.getElementById("qz-results");
  var elFinal = document.getElementById("qz-final");
  var elBreakdown = document.getElementById("qz-breakdown");
  var elMissed = document.getElementById("qz-missed");
  var elRestart = document.getElementById("qz-restart");
  var elForm = document.getElementById("qz-form");

  var idx = 0, score = 0, locked = false, missed = [], byTheme = {};

  function esc(s) {
    return String(s).replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;").replace(/>/g, "&gt;");
  }

  function render(initial) {
    var q = Q[idx];
    locked = false;
    elTheme.textContent = q.theme;
    elCount.textContent = "Question " + (idx + 1) + " of " + Q.length;
    elScore.textContent = "Score " + score;
    elFill.style.width = ((idx + 1) / Q.length * 100) + "%";
    elStem.textContent = q.stem;
    elFeedback.innerHTML = "";
    elOptions.innerHTML = q.options.map(function (opt, i) {
      return '<label class="qz-option" for="qz-opt-' + i + '">' +
        '<input type="radio" name="qz-answer" id="qz-opt-' + i + '" value="' + i + '">' +
        '<span>' + esc(opt) + '</span><span class="qz-mark" aria-hidden="true"></span></label>';
    }).join("");
    elCheck.hidden = false;
    elCheck.disabled = true;
    elNext.hidden = true;
    elNext.textContent = (idx === Q.length - 1) ? "See results" : "Next question";
    if (!initial) elStem.focus();
  }

  function chosen() {
    var picked = elOptions.querySelector('input[name="qz-answer"]:checked');
    return picked ? Number(picked.value) : -1;
  }

  elOptions.addEventListener("change", function () {
    if (!locked) elCheck.disabled = chosen() < 0;
  });

  elForm.addEventListener("submit", function (e) { e.preventDefault(); });

  elCheck.addEventListener("click", function () {
    if (locked) return;
    var pick = chosen();
    if (pick < 0) return;
    locked = true;
    var q = Q[idx];
    var right = pick === q.answer;
    if (right) score++;
    if (!byTheme[q.theme]) byTheme[q.theme] = { right: 0, total: 0 };
    byTheme[q.theme].total++;
    if (right) byTheme[q.theme].right++;
    else missed.push({ n: idx + 1, stem: q.stem, href: q.href, hrefText: q.hrefText });

    var labels = elOptions.querySelectorAll(".qz-option");
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
      var input = labels[i].querySelector("input");
      input.disabled = true;
      labels[i].classList.add("is-locked");
      if (i === q.answer) {
        labels[i].classList.add("is-correct");
        labels[i].querySelector(".qz-mark").textContent = "✓";
      } else if (i === pick) {
        labels[i].classList.add("is-wrong");
        labels[i].querySelector(".qz-mark").textContent = "✗";
      }
    }

    elScore.textContent = "Score " + score;
    elFeedback.innerHTML =
      '<p class="qz-explain"><span class="qz-verdict ' + (right ? "qz-verdict-yes" : "qz-verdict-no") + '">' +
      (right ? "✓ Correct" : "✗ Not quite") + '</span>' + esc(q.explain) +
      '<a class="qz-source" href="' + q.href + '">Read the source: ' + esc(q.hrefText) + ' →</a>' +
      (q.href2 ? '<a class="qz-source" href="' + q.href2 + '">Also: ' + esc(q.hrefText2) + ' →</a>' : '') +
      '</p>';
    elCheck.hidden = true;
    elNext.hidden = false;
    elFeedback.focus();
  });

  elNext.addEventListener("click", function () {
    if (idx < Q.length - 1) { idx++; render(); elStem.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" }); }
    else finish();
  });

  function finish() {
    shell.hidden = true;
    elResults.hidden = false;
    var pct = Math.round(score / Q.length * 100);
    elFinal.textContent = score + " out of " + Q.length + " (" + pct + "%).";
    var rows = Object.keys(byTheme).map(function (t) {
      return '<div class="qz-breakdown-row"><span>' + esc(t) + '</span><strong>' +
        byTheme[t].right + " / " + byTheme[t].total + "</strong></div>";
    });
    elBreakdown.innerHTML = rows.join("");
    if (missed.length) {
      elMissed.innerHTML = "<h4>Worth rereading</h4><ol>" + missed.map(function (m) {
        return "<li>Q" + m.n + ". " + esc(m.stem) +
          '<br><a href="' + m.href + '">' + esc(m.hrefText) + " →</a></li>";
      }).join("") + "</ol>";
    } else {
      elMissed.innerHTML = "<p>Nothing missed — every answer matched the source.</p>";
    }
    document.getElementById("qz-results-title").focus();
  }

  elRestart.addEventListener("click", function () {
    idx = 0; score = 0; missed = []; byTheme = {};
    elResults.hidden = true;
    shell.hidden = false;
    render();
    elStem.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" });
  });

  document.getElementById("qz-results-title").setAttribute("tabindex", "-1");
  elStem.setAttribute("tabindex", "-1");
  elFeedback.setAttribute("tabindex", "-1");
  render(true);
})();
</script>
